triage.title: Headline retainer
triage.detail: `java.lang.Thread` (a single object) retains 5.5 MB (48.8% of reachable heap).

triage.title: Concentration
triage.detail: diffuse — retention is spread across multiple roots, so there is no single object to free.

triage.title: Shape
triage.detail: deep (retention flows through long dominator chains — often nested collections or linked structures) — 90% of objects within depth 8, max depth 28.

triage.title: One leak or many
triage.detail: the single biggest object, `java.lang.Thread`, retains 48.8% and the top 10 retain 84.3% of the heap; 6 object(s) each hold >=1%.

triage.title: Thread pinning
triage.detail: thread `main` retains 5.5 MB (48.8% of heap) and pins 329 thread-local roots — a live thread is holding memory alive.

triage.title: Off-heap (DirectByteBuffer)
triage.detail: 134.3 MB of native memory is held by live DirectByteBuffers — not counted in heap size but can dominate RSS.

triage.title: Fixed per-object header overhead
triage.detail: 334,875 objects × 12 B header = 3.8 MB (34.1% of heap) is consumed by JVM object headers alone — consider value types, primitive arrays, or fewer wrapper objects.

triage.title: Empty-collection cemetery
triage.detail: 2,943 of 3,891 tracked collections (75.6%) are empty (size == 0) — pre-allocated but never populated containers waste object-header overhead; consider lazy initialisation or null.

triage.title: Collection waste not analyzed
triage.detail: _Collection waste not analyzed — re-run with `--collections` to check for wasted capacity._
